authoredNote: Expectations written from the Svelte/JavaScript rule that an object literal's `key` field is a WRITE and its `value` is a READ, from the grammar's own shape (probed: an attribute expression value is `expression > svelte_raw_text`, and a quoted attribute value wraps the same `expression`), and from the oracle that found the defect — it derives the read set from a REAL parse of each fragment, where a `pair`'s `key` field is not a read. Line pins and `meta.templateReadLines` read off the post-fix run and checked against the fixture's text: shorthand 47, computed key 50, ternaries 53/54, nested ternary 57, spread 60, receiver 66. The ARRAY pins carry the key assertions — the graph contract is ONE edge per `type|source|target`, so `foo` is published once at its LAST site and the list is the only place its other sites are stated; `[47,54,66]` therefore proves that line 43 (`{{ foo: true }}`, a key) is NOT a read site, which a `line_number` forbid could not have proved.
rationale: JOB 2 of the svelte ontology pass. Three read-site rules in one fixture because all three are decisions the character walker has to earn. (1) An object-literal KEY is not a read: 49 edges in 38 of the 6,439 corpus files named a key the template never reads, and the worst of them resolved — `chart-pie-stacked.svelte` published `tooltip` because the same file declares `{#snippet tooltip()}`. (2) The key rule has to be TERNARY-AWARE or it eats real reads, because `? :` and `: ` are the same character: lines 53, 54 and 57 pin that both ternary arms publish. (3) A SPREAD argument is a read: `[...foo]` was suppressed by the receiver-only dot rule because the token before `foo` is a dot — runtime-legacy/samples/array-literal-spread-deopt published nothing for `foo`. The forbids pin the three shapes a widened rule would get wrong: an object key, a computed-key word, and a member leaf.

forbidRelationships.comment: `{{ month: "january" }}` on 44 and `{{ month: cond ? alpha : beta }}` on 57 — `month` is the KEY of a written property in both. Publishing it is the false read this fixture exists for; the corpus's worst case RESOLVED, because chart-pie-stacked.svelte declares `{#snippet tooltip()}` and so published `uses -> tooltip` off a Recharts config key.
`rows.length` on 63 — a member LEAF on a member is not a component-level read; the collector's dot rule skips it and must keep skipping it
the `{#each [...list] as item}` BINDING is a template-local; only the collection `list` publishes. The spread fix widened the READ side and must not widen the binding side.
